content:
In a playful post on X, Apple CEO Tim Cook shared a short video showing Pikachu running around Apple Park during a visit from the Pokémon team. Watch the video below.

Pikachu visits Apple Park

Apple welcomed the Pokémon team to Apple Park today and decided to have a bit of fun with the occasion.

In a video shared to X, Cook responded to the visit by joking that the day's agenda was to introduce the Pokémon team to incoming CEO John Ternus, "talk about games," and "politely ask Pikachu not to go in the pond."

Cook added: "Two out of three was achieved."

The accompanying video shows Pikachu wandering around Apple Park, attempting to reach for apples on an apple tree, and eventually heading toward the pond. Cook, Ternus, and Tsunekazu Ishihara, CEO of The Pokémon Company, subsequently joined in.

Although neither Apple nor The Pokémon Company has revealed further details about the visit, the video is quite fun and worth 30 seconds of your time.

A few weeks before Apple met with The Pokémon Company CEO, a Sensor Tower report noted that mobile gaming revenue declined 4.5% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026.

A few weeks before Apple met with The Pokémon Company, Apple acknowledged that weaker mobile gaming performance had begun to weigh on App Store growth.

During the Q3 2026 earnings call, Apple CFO Kevan Parekh specifically cited "headwinds in mobile gaming" as one of the factors affecting that quarter's App Store performance — you can learn more about that here.
